content_voiceover: The HAVEN trials are the pivotal studies establishing emicizumab's efficacy across different hemophilia A populations, and boards may ask you to match trial number to population. HAVEN 1 studied adults and adolescents with inhibitors, showing weekly prophylaxis dropped the annualized bleed rate from 23.3 with no prophylaxis down to 2.9. HAVEN 2 studied children with inhibitors, achieving even lower bleed rates, around 0.2 to 2.2 depending on dosing interval, with zero-bleed rates up to 90 percent on every-two-week dosing. HAVEN 3 studied adults and adolescents without inhibitors, again showing dramatic reduction from 38.2 down to about 1.3 to 1.5. HAVEN 4 tested an extended every-four-week, six milligram per kilogram regimen across patients with or without inhibitors, landing at an ABR of 4.5, demonstrating that even monthly dosing provides meaningful protection. The overarching theme is that emicizumab prophylaxis, regardless of dosing interval, dramatically outperforms no prophylaxis in every population tested.
keypoints: HAVEN 1: adults/adolescents WITH inhibitors, ABR 2.9 vs 23.3 no prophylaxis
HAVEN 2: children with inhibitors, lowest ABR, up to 90% zero-bleed rate
HAVEN 3: adults/adolescents WITHOUT inhibitors, ABR ~1.3-1.5 vs 38.2
HAVEN 4: extended every-4-week dosing (6 mg/kg), ABR 4.5, inhibitor status either
keypoint_voiceover: Match the HAVEN trials by population: HAVEN 1 is inhibitor-positive adults, HAVEN 2 is inhibitor-positive children, HAVEN 3 is inhibitor-negative adults and adolescents, and HAVEN 4 tests extended every-four-week dosing regardless of inhibitor status. All show large annualized bleed rate reductions versus no prophylaxis.
